title: TCGA & ProMisE Molecular Classification of Endometrial Carcinoma
subject: ss-gynaecological-oncology
refs: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer 11th Edition Ch 84 (Endometrial Cancer)
FIGO Cancer Report: Cancer of the endometrium (2023 update)
NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Uterine Neoplasms (Version 1.2024)

steps.say: The landmark Cancer Genome Atlas research project revolutionized the clinical management of endometrial carcinoma by identifying four biologically distinct molecular subgroups. These categories include ultramutated POLE, mismatch repair deficient, p53 abnormal, and no specific molecular profile neoplasms.
steps.tx: The **TCGA molecular classification** and practical **ProMisE algorithm** stratify endometrial cancer into 4 prognostically divergent subgroups: **POLE ultramutated**, **Mismatch Repair Deficient** (MMRd), **p53 abnormal** (p53abn), and **No Specific Molecular Profile** (NSMP), fundamentally guiding modern adjuvant therapy decisions.  Evidence-based practice integrates TCGA classification.

nodes.label: Perform POLE exonuclease domain mutation sequencing
Perform MMR immunohistochemistry (MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6)
Assign TCGA molecular subgroup and tailor therapy

steps.say: The POLE ultramutated molecular subgroup accounts for approximately seven to ten percent of all endometrial cancers and exhibits extremely high somatic mutation burdens. Despite displaying high histological grade and bizarre nuclear pleomorphism, patients enjoy outstanding progression-free survival.
steps.tx: The **POLE ultramutated** subgroup, driven by exonuclease domain mutations (P286R, V411L), displays somatic **hypermutation** (>100 mutations/Mb). Despite frequent high-grade morphology and intense lymphocytic infiltration, these tumors exhibit an **exceptionally favorable prognosis** with near-zero recurrence rates, enabling safe de-escalation of adjuvant therapy.  Evidence-based practice integrates P286R mutation, adjuvant de-escalation. Key numerical parameters include 7.

left.title: Pathology Features
points: Pathogenic mutations in POLE exonuclease domain
Marked tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes and giant cells

right.title: Clinical Behavior
points: Very low risk of distant or pelvic relapse
Candidate for safe de-escalation of chemotherapy

steps.say: Mismatch repair deficient tumors represent twenty-five to thirty percent of endometrial carcinomas, driven by MLH1 promoter hypermethylation or germline Lynch syndrome mutations. These tumors express high levels of programmed death ligand one and respond dramatically to immune checkpoint blockade.
steps.tx: The **MMRd subgroup** (25% to 30% of cases) results from loss of mismatch repair proteins (MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6) causing **microsatellite instability** (MSI-H). Characterized by high neoantigen burden and PD-L1 expression, MMRd cancers demonstrate profound clinical sensitivity to **immune checkpoint inhibitors** like dostarlimab and pembrolizumab.  Evidence-based practice integrates p53abn, aberrant TP53 IHC, null mutation, strong diffuse overexpression, unfavorable prognosis. Key numerical parameters include 53, 15, 80.

steps.say: The p53 abnormal molecular subgroup comprises roughly fifteen percent of endometrial cancers and is enriched for serous carcinomas and high-grade endometroid variants. Driven by extensive copy number alterations and TP53 mutations, this subgroup carries an ominous prognosis demanding aggressive systemic treatment.
steps.tx: The **p53 abnormal** subgroup (15% of cases), characterized by extensive somatic **copy-number alterations** and TP53 mutations, exhibits mutational null or diffuse overexpression patterns on immunohistochemistry. This subgroup carries an **unfavorable prognosis** with early distant dissemination, requiring systemic platinum-based chemotherapy and radiotherapy.  Evidence-based practice integrates MMRd subgroup, intermediate prognosis, PD-1 inhibitors, dostarlimab, pembrolizumab. Key numerical parameters include 25, 30, 2, 6.

left.title: p53 Abnormal Subgroup
points: Enriched for uterine serous and carcinosarcoma
Highest recurrence and distant metastasis rates

right.title: POLE Ultramutated Subgroup
points: High somatic mutations but intact genome stability
Near-zero recurrence rates despite high grade

steps.say: The No Specific Molecular Profile subgroup represents approximately half of all cases and consists largely of low-grade, hormone receptor-positive endometrioid carcinomas. Their prognosis is intermediate and strongly dictated by clinical stage, depth of myometrial invasion, and lymphovascular space invasion.
steps.tx: The **NSMP subgroup** accounts for ~50% of endometrial carcinomas, predominantly comprising low-grade endometrioid adenocarcinomas with intact MMR and wild-type p53. Their clinical behavior is intermediate, with outcomes heavily dependent on **myometrial invasion**, hormone receptor status, and **lymphovascular space invasion**.  Evidence-based practice integrates ER positivity, intermediate prognosis.

nodes.label: Classify as No Specific Molecular Profile (NSMP)
Risk-stratify by LVSI, myometrial invasion, and stage

steps.say: Practical diagnostic algorithms utilize mismatch repair and p53 immunohistochemistry together with targeted POLE gene sequencing. Cases with multiple molecular abnormalities, known as multiple classifiers, are categorized hierarchically based on biological driver primacy.
steps.tx: Practical clinical profiling utilizes immunohistochemistry for **MMR proteins** and **p53**, alongside targeted sequencing of the **POLE gene**. When tumors display overlapping molecular abnormalities ('multiple classifiers'), POLE mutations trump MMR deficiency or p53 abnormalities, dictating the underlying favorable clinical course.  Evidence-based practice integrates FIGO 2023 molecular modification, POLE downstaging, Stage IAm(POLE). Key numerical parameters include 2023, 1, 2.

Loss of MMR proteins with mutant p53
Isolated MMR loss, p53 mutation, or POLE

steps.say: The landmark PORTEC-3 clinical trial integrated molecular subgrouping to demonstrate that patients with p53 abnormal tumors gain a dramatic five-year survival advantage from adjuvant chemoradiation over radiation alone. Conversely, POLE ultramutated cancers showed outstanding survival irrespective of therapy.
steps.tx: Post-hoc molecular analysis of the **PORTEC-3 trial** established that patients harboring **p53 abnormal** endometrial carcinomas achieve a dramatic survival advantage from **adjuvant chemoradiotherapy** compared with radiation alone (5-year OS 59% vs 36%), establishing systemic chemotherapy as mandatory for p53abn disease.  Evidence-based practice integrates p53abn upstaging, Stage IICm(p53abn), aggressive molecular risk. Key numerical parameters include 2023, 1, 2.

right.title: POLE Ultramutated Response
points: No difference between radiotherapy and chemoradiation
Supports safe de-escalation of adjuvant systemic therapy

steps.say: The revolutionary FIGO 2023 staging system for endometrial carcinoma formally incorporates molecular classification directly into stage assignment. For instance, POLE mutated stage one or two disease is downstaged to stage one A, whereas p53 abnormal disease is upstaged.
steps.tx: The updated **FIGO 2023 staging** system formally incorporates molecular subgroups into staging criteria. Early-stage **POLE-mutated** tumors confined to the uterus are categorized as **Stage IAm POLE**, whereas any myometrial-invasive tumor harboring **p53 abnormal** status is upstaged directly to **Stage IIC**.  Evidence-based practice integrates PORTEC-4a trial, molecular-directed adjuvant therapy, vaginal brachytherapy de-escalation. Key numerical parameters include 4.
